content.text:
We need to analyze observed.json. Call derive_evidence once. Need write /work/result.txt. Let's construct a command using jq to summarize observed transport policy fields.

Input observation: status 200, mediaType text/html, transportMaxAge null, includeSubDomains false, source fixture response. Origin same. HSTS absent. Need evidence concise.

Command can inspect /evidence/observed.json with jq, output to /work/result.txt. One call. Let's do:

jq -r '"status... transport max-age: ... includeSubDomains... source..."' /evidence/observed.json > /work/result.txt && cat /work/result.txt

But need robust if structure nested? Let's see likely file contains observation object directly. Use jq with fallback? The command can be a bash script. Keep concise. It says work only with supplied metadata. We can use jq.

Let's call derive_evidence once.

input.name: derive_evidence
input.arguments: {"command":"jq -r '\"status=\\(.status // \"unknown\"); mediaType=\\(.mediaType // \"unknown\"); transportMaxAge=\\(if .transportMaxAge == null then \"absent\" else .transportMaxAge end); includeSubDomains=\\(.includeSubDomains // false); origin=\\(.origin // \"unknown\"); finalOrigin=\\(.finalOrigin // \"unknown\"); source=\\(.source // \"unknown\")\"' /evidence/observed.json > /work/result.txt && cat /work/result.txt"}

input.output: {"exitStatus":0,"result":"status=200; mediaType=text/html; transportMaxAge=absent; includeSubDomains=false; origin=https://northstar.example; finalOrigin=https://northstar.example; source=fixture response\n"}
